question: Epicurus sorted human desires into three kinds. Where did he put the desire for honours and statues of yourself?
answer: Neither natural nor necessary. An ancient note on his Principal Doctrines gives the examples: drink when thirsty is natural and necessary; costly food natural but unnecessary; crowns and statues neither, because they spring from empty opinion and have no limit. A follower count has no level that would ever be enough.
move: A desire with no natural stopping point will never be satisfied.
ask: Which of my wants has no finish line, and what would enough look like?
trap: Natural but unnecessary, since wanting respect feels deeply human.
reference: Inwood & Gerson (trans.), The Epicurus Reader, Hackett, 1994, Principal Doctrines 29
